what_its_for: Capmatinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a certain type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in adults. It works specifically for lung cancer that has a mutation (change) in a gene called MET exon 14 skipping. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_to_take: Take capmatinib by mouth (as a tablet) twice a day, about 12 hours apart. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, break, or chew it. Try to take it at the same times every day to keep a steady amount in your body.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 mg (two 200 mg tablets) taken twice daily, approximately every 12 hours. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on how you tolerate the medicine or if you have side effects. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if your next scheduled dose is more than 6 hours away. If your next dose is in 6 hours or less, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store capmatinib tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Store out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids, vitamins, or supplements that contain calcium, magnesium, aluminum, or iron within 2 hours before or after taking capmatinib, as they can reduce how well the medicine works. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Avoid sunlight and UV rays (like tanning beds) as this medicine can make your skin very sensitive to the sun — use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines (prescription, over-the-counter, and herbal products) you take, as many drugs can interact with capmatinib, including blood thinners like warfarin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: shortness of breath, chest pain, or a new or worsening cough (could be a serious lung problem called interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis); severe nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, yellowing of your skin or eyes, or dark urine (possible liver problems); swelling of your legs, ankles, or face (fluid buildup/edema); painful, blistering skin rash or sores in your mouth; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination; dizziness or fainting; or any unusual or severe symptoms you are not sure about.
when_it_works: Capmatinib may start working within the first few weeks, but it can take several weeks to months before you fully notice its benefits. Your doctor will monitor you with regular imaging scans and blood tests to check how the medicine is working. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Capmatinib can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for 1 week after the last dose. Liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have moderate or severe liver disease. Kidney problems: Dose adjustment is generally not needed for mild to moderate kidney disease, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustment is required based on age alone, but your doctor will monitor you closely.
